B. Accomplishments under Stated Goals Task 1 Project management efforts were exerted throughout the period of the project to ensure efficiency and timely reporting – including but not limited to all activities outlined in the SOPO under Task 1. Additionally, we set up internal processes and meetings to run the project, as well as a budgeting and accounting system to maintain financial compliance. We’ve worked with Oak Ridge National Laboratory to set up a contract, as well as to split the tasks according to our project proposal and allocated respective budgets. Task 2 The goals are to (1) understand the various ways in which chemicals used in the DAC process are lost, and (2) to devise ways to prevent these losses. To achieve these goals, thorough review of the chemical literature was conducted followed by the development of methods to measure decomposition of both the bis(iminoguanidine) and amino acids in our system that may occur via the mechanisms found in the literature. To better quantify chemical degradation, we developed experimental test bench systems to subject the chemicals to conditions that simulate a significant amount of cycles in a single experiment, enabling us to more accurately measure the cumulative degradation that would otherwise be obscured by 4 the more significant transfer losses within a single cycle. Several experimental setups were used to study potential losses. Losses During Absorption: To study the amino acid losses during absorption, we utilized the existing ORNL wind The long-term sorbent loss experiment was conducted for a significant amount of hours using a representative amino acid solution. The experiment was conducted at room temperature, with a set air velocity through the contactor. The inlet CO concentration was approximately 400 ppm throughout the 2 experiment. Throughout the experiment, samples of the aqueous solution were taken approximately every 8 hours. This was done by stopping the circulation in the wind tunnel and allowing the solution to fully drain to the solution tank An initial analysis of the concentration of amino acid over time during the extended sorbent loss experiment has been conducted. For analysis, the lower collection of datapoints in each series - representing samples taken after the aqueous solution has been re-diluted to the initial volume - is the most meaningful, as variable amounts of water evaporation take place during the experiment depending on the ambient conditions. The analysis was outlined but not completed due to the termination of the project.
